platform: Windows 11 (26200), debug build with embedded frontend, isolated test mode (ADR 0003), WebView2 over CDP
host: a WSL2 Ubuntu VM on the same PC (separate OS, sshd and user database), not a separate machine; sshd on 127.0.0.1:2222, key-only, the key in the Windows ssh-agent
method: Real webview of an isolated instance (fresh data folder and WebView2 profile, started from PowerShell with no WEBVIEW2_* variable, local engine pinned by MUSE_DESKTOP_TEST_SIDECAR), the system OpenSSH client and the user's ssh agent. App actions go through the UI (Settings form, welcome picker, composer, work panel, Reconnect, the conversation's actions dialog); the native git, terminal and files commands are invoked directly only to show they refuse. Remote facts come from a separate ssh session as the same user (stat and cat of the file, grep of the workspace, pgrep of `muse serve` with its working folder and environment). The app's ssh child is found by its command line and parent (Win32_Process) and killed by PID with taskkill /F; the app itself is closed with WM_CLOSE.
limits: The host is a VM on the same PC: a real network (latency, a link dropped by a router rather than by a killed process) is not measured.
The remote engine is 1.3.0, the fixed binary installed on that host; the local test sidecar is the native 1.4.2 and no local conversation runs here.
summary: M4-07 proved natively on Windows, in the isolated test mode, against a WSL2 Ubuntu VM on the same PC: the target typed in Settings, a new conversation started on its ssh:// key, the system OpenSSH spawned as the app's child, a Muse 1.3.0 engine on linux handshaking over it. One live turn wrote a file with write_file in the remote folder, read back over a separate ssh session. Changes, Terminal, Files and the native git, terminal and files commands refused. The ssh child killed by PID left an honest Disconnected state; Reconnect resumed the same session over a new link, the history was read back, and a second turn recalled a code said only in the first prompt, with no tool call. Four failed starts each gave one actionable sentence, known_hosts byte-identical. The app closed on WM_CLOSE leaving no ssh child and no remote muse serve. No product defect found; one change made before the proof (d7629c2): in test mode, a configured ssh:// target is reached over the system ssh, every local engine stays the test sidecar.
observations: The two prompts (harness constants PROMPT_WRITE and PROMPT_RECALL): the first asks for remote-proof.txt holding the marker, written with the file tool, and gives a second code to keep but never write or use in a command; the second asks for that code without any tool.

The first link death was resumed by the app on its own (resume-on-open: one silent attempt per conversation per run, already recorded in m0-05-questions.json and left unchanged); the second left the conversation Disconnected with Reconnect and the composer's Send disabled. Each death added one system line to the transcript.

The unknown-host-key start took 10.2 s, the others 0.5 to 2.6 s: localhost resolves to ::1 first, where port 2222 does not answer, and ssh waits its ConnectTimeout (10 s) before 127.0.0.1, whose key is unknown under that name (checked afterwards with ssh -v, known_hosts unchanged).
